intro:
Tracking the gold price in Australia today gives investors, SMSF trustees, and jewellery shoppers a dependable benchmark in Australian dollars. As one of the world's largest gold-producing nations and home to the globally accredited Perth Mint, Australia sits at the forefront of physical bullion refining, sovereign coin minting, and Asia-Pacific precious metals trade.

Whether you are checking the Australia gold rate today to buy GST-free 24K Perth Mint Kangaroo coins and cast bars, monitoring the 22K gold price Australia per gram and per tola for bridal jewellery, or valuing 18K and 9K pieces, our live tables and interactive calculator above display real-time AUD prices across every standard weight and purity.

sections.h2: Gold Rate in Australia Today: How Live AUD Spot Prices Work per Ounce and Gram
paragraphs: When you check the gold price today Australia tables on this page, you are viewing the live international bullion benchmark converted directly into Australian dollars (AUD). Because wholesale bullion trades globally in US dollars while local refiners, bullion dealers, and jewellers in Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Brisbane, and Adelaide transact in Aussie dollars, the live australia gold rate moves dynamically with both international spot trading and the AUD/USD exchange rate.

In the Australian precious metals market, the troy ounce (approximately 31.1 grams) is the standard unit for quoting wholesale spot prices, Perth Mint bullion coins, and mining production figures. At the retail counter, however, metric grams—specifically 1 gram, 10 grams, 100 grams, and 1000 grams (1 kilogram)—are used daily to price minted gold bars, cast ingots, and fine jewellery.

Remember that the live spot rate represents raw wholesale metal before fabrication. Physical bullion coins, sealed assay bars, and retail jewellery always include minting or crafting charges, security logistics, and dealer margins above the baseline AUD spot figure shown in our live chart.
bullets: Australian gold prices are quoted in Australian dollars (AUD) and reflect both global USD spot prices and the Aussie dollar exchange rate.
The troy ounce (31.1 grams) is the benchmark for Australian bullion coins, while per-gram pricing is standard for jewellery and fractional bars.
Australia's position in the Asia-Pacific time zone means live local trading is active before European and North American markets open.
Use the live table and calculator above to check exact AUD values for 1 gram, 10 grams, 1 troy ounce, or 1 kilogram.

sections.h2: Which Gold Purity to Buy in Australia: 24K (9999 Fine), 22K, 18K, 14K, and 9K
paragraphs: For Australian bullion investors and Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs), 24K pure gold (stamped 9999 or 99.99% pure) is the gold standard. Both The Perth Mint and the Royal Australian Mint strike their flagship investment coins and bullion bars in 99.99% pure gold. Buying 24K (9999 fine) ensures maximum metal density, universal international recognition, and full compliance with Australian GST-free precious metal rules.

In Australia's vibrant multicultural jewellery districts across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Perth, the 22K gold price Australia per gram and per 10 grams is closely followed by families shopping for high-purity wedding sets, bangles, and heirloom pieces. Stamped 916 to signify 91.67% pure gold, 22K offers a warm, rich yellow glow while adding just enough alloy strength to hold intricate traditional craftsmanship.

In mainstream Australian fine jewellery boutiques and chain stores, 18K gold (stamped 750) and 9K gold (stamped 375) have historically been the two most popular purities, with 14K gold (stamped 585) also widely available. While 18K is favoured for luxury engagement rings and fine gemstone settings, 9K gold remains an affordable, hard-wearing staple across Australian shopping centres for everyday chains, earrings, and signet rings.
bullets: 24K (9999 fine): Pure investment-grade gold used in Australian Kangaroo coins, Lunar Series coins, and Perth Mint bars.
22K (916 fine): High-karat alloy prized across Australian cultural jewellery hubs for traditional bridal and heirloom ornaments.
18K (750 fine): Premium Australian fine jewellery standard combining rich colour with durable stone-setting strength.
14K (585 fine) and 9K (375 fine): Tough, scratch-resistant alloys widely sold in mainstream Australian retail jewellers.

sections.h2: The Perth Mint, Australian Kangaroo Coins, and Cast vs. Minted Bars
paragraphs: Australia is home to The Perth Mint, one of the world's largest and most prestigious LBMA-accredited refineries, owned and guaranteed by the Government of Western Australia. Because Australia mines vast quantities of primary gold directly from domestic deposits in Western Australia and across the continent, local investors enjoy direct access to freshly refined bullion coins and bars with world-class quality assurance.

The flagship sovereign bullion coin of Australia is the 24K Australian Gold Kangaroo, alongside the highly sought-after Australian Lunar Series and products from the Royal Australian Mint. Unlike many foreign bullion coins whose designs never change, the Australian Gold Kangaroo features an updated kangaroo artistry each cycle while remaining a pure 9999 fine legal tender bullion coin, giving it strong appeal among both bullion savers and global collectors.

When choosing between coins, minted bars, and cast bars in Australia, consider how premiums scale with size. Minted Perth Mint bars arrive sealed in tamper-evident assay cards from 1 gram up to 100 grams and make attractive, easily verified gifts or fractional holdings. Traditional Perth Mint and ABC Bullion cast bars—available in 1 oz, half-ounce, 100 gram, 10 oz, and 1 kilogram sizes—skip ornate packaging to offer some of the lowest fabrication premiums over the live AUD spot price.
bullets: The Perth Mint is owned by the Government of Western Australia and refines a large share of the region's newly mined gold.
Australian Gold Kangaroo and Lunar Series coins are struck in 99.99% pure (24K) gold with Australian legal tender status.
Cast gold bars in 1 oz, 100 gram, and 1 kilogram sizes offer Australian investors the lowest cost per gram over spot.
Minted bars sealed in serialized CertiCard assay packaging provide easy authentication for fractional weights.

sections.h2: Australian GST Rules on Investment Gold vs. Retail Jewellery
paragraphs: Tax treatment is a major factor separating investment bullion from decorative jewellery in Australia. Under Australian Goods and Services Tax (GST) legislation, precious metal qualifies as GST-free investment bullion if it is in a tradeable bar, wafer, or coin form with a fineness of at least 99.5% pure gold (which encompasses all 24K 999 and 9999 gold products). As a result, buying 24K Australian Gold Kangaroo coins, Lunar coins, or 9999 gold bars from a bullion dealer incurs zero GST.

By contrast, gold coins or medallions with a purity below the 99.5% threshold—such as historic or foreign 22K coins (91.67% fine)—do not meet the Australian Taxation Office definition of GST-free precious metal unless specific collectible or second-hand rules apply, meaning they can attract GST. That is why Australian bullion investors and SMSF trustees focus almost exclusively on 24K (9999 fine) coins and bars.

All finished gold jewellery sold at retail in Australia—whether crafted in 9K, 14K, 18K, 22K, or 24K—is classified as a taxable consumer good and includes GST in the retail price, on top of the jeweller's craftsmanship and showroom markups.
bullets: Gold bullion bars and coins with at least 99.5% purity (all 24K 9999 products) are exempt from GST in Australia.
24K Perth Mint Kangaroo coins, Lunar coins, and 9999 cast or minted bars are completely GST-free.
Physical 24K bullion is widely held inside Australian Self-Managed Super Funds (SMSFs) subject to storage and audit rules.
Retail gold jewellery of any karat (including 22K bridal ornaments and 18K/9K rings) is subject to Australian GST.

sections.h2: Gold Weights Used in Australia: Troy Ounces, Grams, 10 Grams, and Tolas
paragraphs: Australian buyers regularly work with both troy ounces and metric grams. Whenever you check the gold price today Australia per ounce, the quote refers to one troy ounce of 31.1 grams—not the standard avoirdupois ounce. Australian bullion coins are commonly sold in 1 oz, half-ounce, quarter-ounce, and tenth-ounce troy weights.

For bars and retail jewellery, metric weights are universal across Australia. Investors frequently buy 1 gram, 5 gram, 10 gram, 20 gram, 50 gram, and 100 gram minted bars, while larger portfolios and SMSFs favour 250 gram, 500 gram, and 1000 gram (1 kilogram) cast bars for their ultra-tight premiums over the spot rate.

In multicultural shopping precincts across Western Sydney (such as Harris Park and Parramatta), Melbourne (Dandenong and CBD), Brisbane, and Perth, buyers also track the gold price in Australia per tola (approximately 11.66 grams) and per 10 grams when shopping for 22K jewellery. Many diaspora buyers also compare the gold price in Australia vs India or check rates in Indian rupees to evaluate whether to buy wedding jewellery locally in Australia or overseas.
bullets: 1 Troy Ounce (31.1 grams): The benchmark weight for Perth Mint bullion coins and live wholesale AUD spot quotes.
1 Gram and 10 Grams: Standard metric units for minted assay bars, scrap valuations, and 22K jewellery pricing.
1 Tola (11.66 grams): Traditional measure referenced in Australian South Asian 22K jewellery boutiques.
1 Kilogram (1000 grams): Institutional cast bar size widely used by wholesale buyers and Australian SMSF portfolios.

sections.h2: Why Australian Bullion Dealer and Jewellery Shop Prices Differ from Spot
paragraphs: When comparing the live gold rate in Australia per gram on this page with quotes at a bullion showroom in Sydney's Martin Place, Melbourne's Collins Street, or Perth, you will see a modest gap between the raw spot rate and physical product prices. For 24K bullion bars and coins, dealers add a fabrication and distribution premium that covers refining to 9999 purity, minting dies, assay certification, insured courier delivery, and dealer operating margins.

In Australian retail jewellery stores, the retail tag reflects much more than raw gold content. Mainstream 9K, 14K, and 18K jewellery is priced per piece, bundling design labour, gemstone setting, retail showroom rent, marketing, and Australian GST. Consequently, the retail price of a boutique 9K or 18K chain is several multiples of its raw karat melt value.

In specialist 22K cultural jewellery boutiques across Sydney and Melbourne, pricing is usually transparent and formula-based: the store multiplies the net gram weight of the piece by its daily 22K board rate, adds a craftsmanship making charge per gram, and includes GST. Checking the live 22K gold price AUD gram in our table before visiting the shop lets you verify the raw metal component and negotiate making charges with confidence.
bullets: Bullion dealer premiums cover 9999 refining, minting, security packaging, and insured domestic shipping.
Cast bars carry lower fabrication premiums per gram than minted assay bars or sovereign coins.
22K jewellery boutiques in Australia charge the live 22K metal weight plus making charges and GST.
Always review both the buy price and sell-back price on an Australian bullion dealer's live board.

sections.h2: What Moves the Gold Price in Australia: The Aussie Dollar, RBA, and Mining Output
paragraphs: The gold price in Australian dollars is renowned among domestic portfolio managers for acting as a natural shock absorber during global market downturns. Because the Australian dollar is a pro-cyclical commodity currency closely tied to global industrial growth and iron ore demand, the Aussie dollar often softens against the US dollar whenever global financial stress or recession fears emerge. At those exact moments, safe-haven buying typically lifts the US dollar gold price—and the weaker AUD exchange rate amplifies the gain in Australian dollar terms.

Conversely, during periods when a strong Australian dollar rallies against the greenback, local AUD gold prices may remain steady even if USD gold climbs. Therefore, tracking the live AUD gold rate directly is essential for Australian residents rather than relying solely on US dollar financial headlines.

Domestic monetary policy set by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), domestic inflation expectations, real yields on Australian government bonds, and central bank bullion purchases across the Asia-Pacific region also shape the daily trend of gold in Australia.
bullets: The AUD/USD exchange rate acts as a natural buffer, often lifting AUD gold prices when global risk sentiment weakens.
Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) interest rate decisions and local CPI inflation data influence domestic investor demand.
Australian gold mining companies on the ASX benchmark their domestic operating margins against the live AUD ounce price.
Strong physical demand across Asian trading hours directly supports liquidity during the Australian business day.

sections.h2: Practical Tips for Buying, Storing, and Selling Gold in Australia
paragraphs: If you are buying gold in Australia for investment or through a Self-Managed Super Fund (SMSF), stick to 24K (9999 fine) GST-free bullion coins and bars from LBMA-accredited refiners such as The Perth Mint or ABC Bullion. SMSF trustees should ensure they receive full tax invoices in the exact name of the superannuation fund, maintain comprehensive insurance, and use audited vault storage or documented security protocols to satisfy annual compliance reviews.

When purchasing 22K or 18K jewellery in Australia, inspect the piece for clear fineness stamps (such as 916 for 22K, 750 for 18K, 585 for 14K, or 375 for 9K) alongside the maker's mark. Ask for an itemised receipt showing the exact gram weight of the gold separate from stones and making charges.

When selling scrap jewellery or bullion in Australia, remember that bullion dealers require valid photo identification under Australian Know Your Customer (KYC) and anti-money-laundering rules. Weigh your 9K, 14K, 18K, or 22K items at home in grams first and check our live AUD calculator above so you know the exact intrinsic melt value before visiting a dealer.
bullets: Choose 24K (9999 fine) Australian coins or accredited bars to enjoy GST-free pricing and tight dealer buy-back spreads.
For SMSF gold holdings, keep formal purchase invoices, serial number records, and compliant insured storage documentation.
Verify fineness stamps (375, 585, 750, 916, or 9999) and request itemised gram weights when buying jewellery.
Bring valid photo ID when selling bullion or scrap gold to an established Australian dealer.

faq.q: Is investment gold exempt from GST in Australia?
faq.a: Yes. Under Australian GST law, gold bars, wafers, and bullion coins with a purity of at least 99.5% fine gold (which includes all 24K 999 and 9999 products) are GST-free. However, lower-purity coins (such as 22K coins) and all retail gold jewellery attract standard Australian GST.

faq.q: Why does the gold price in Australian dollars move differently from the US dollar gold price?
faq.a: The gold price in Australia is calculated by converting the global US dollar spot price into Australian dollars using the live AUD/USD exchange rate. Because the Australian dollar fluctuates against the US dollar, a weaker Aussie dollar will push the local AUD gold price higher even if the USD spot rate stays flat.

faq.q: What is the difference between Perth Mint cast bars and minted bars?
faq.a: Both are refined to 99.99% pure (24K) gold and backed by the Government of Western Australia. Cast bars are poured into moulds with a rustic finish and carry lower fabrication premiums over spot, while minted bars are precision-struck with a mirror finish and sealed inside tamper-evident serialized assay cards.

faq.q: Can I buy physical gold inside an Australian Self-Managed Super Fund (SMSF)?
faq.a: Yes. Australian SMSFs frequently invest in 24K GST-free physical gold bullion bars and coins. Trustees must ensure the bullion is titled in the SMSF's name, insured, never used personally by members, and ideally stored in an audited professional vault that provides annual holding statements.

faq.q: How is 22K gold jewellery priced in Sydney and Melbourne stores?
faq.a: Specialist 22K jewellers in Australia typically weigh the ornament in grams, multiply that weight by the daily 22K gold rate per gram, add a craftsmanship making charge based on design complexity, and apply Australian GST to the final retail total.

faq.q: What does a 375 or 750 stamp mean on Australian gold jewellery?
faq.a: Millesimal fineness stamps indicate parts per thousand of pure gold. A 375 stamp means 9K gold, 585 means 14K gold (58.5% pure), 750 means 18K gold (75% pure), 916 means 22K gold (91.67% pure), and 9999 means 24K pure bullion.

faq.q: How do I calculate the scrap value of old gold jewellery in Australia?
faq.a: Sort your jewellery by its purity stamp, weigh the metal in grams on a digital scale (excluding gemstones), and multiply the weight by the live AUD per-gram rate for that purity in our table above. Reputable bullion dealers in Australian capital cities pay a high percentage of this intrinsic melt value.
